description: The most relevant number of the problem "GDP mismeasurement" of the start page ranking and the potential solution: accounting for one single free service (Facebook) alone would have raised the measured US growth by 0.05 to 0.11 percentage points per year under GDP-B, because free goods enter the national accounts at a price and therefore a value of zero. The solution is a measure of the actual usage instead of the market turnover.

words.name: usage
words.description: how frequently a word, term, or service is used

triples.name: GDP mismeasurement
triples.description: gross domestic product measures the market production and not the benefit, so free goods count as zero and unrepaired damage does not reduce it (concept paper section 11)

triples.name: gross domestic usage
triples.description: a measure of the actual usage instead of the market turnover, so that free goods and avoided damage are part of the result (concept paper section 11)

triples.name: willingness to accept
triples.description: the compensation a person demands to give up a free good, measured with incentive compatible choice experiments

sources.name: Brynjolfsson et al. (2019) GDP-B
sources.description: Brynjolfsson, E., Collis, A., Diewert, W. E., Eggers, F. & Fox, K. J. (2019): GDP-B: Accounting for the Value of New and Free Goods in the Digital Economy. NBER Working Paper 25695.
